pharm: Macrolide; bacterial protein-synthesis inhibitor (50S ribosomal subunit)
summary: Azithromycin is an oral macrolide antibiotic used for mild-to-moderate respiratory, skin, ear and certain genital infections in adults and children 6 months and older. It inhibits bacterial protein synthesis and has a long half-life allowing short courses. A typical adult regimen is 500 mg on Day 1, then 250 mg once daily for 4 days.
indications: Acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis (adults)

dosage.d: 500 mg single dose Day 1, then 250 mg once daily
500 mg Day 1 then 250 mg daily (Days 2-5) OR 500 mg once daily

dosage.c: Genital ulcer disease / non-gonococcal urethritis & cervicitis

dosage.d: 30 mg/kg single dose, OR 10 mg/kg daily x3, OR 10 mg/kg Day 1 then 5 mg/kg Days 2-5
10 mg/kg Day 1 then 5 mg/kg once daily

admin: Take once daily, with or without food
Do not use in pneumonia patients unsuitable for oral therapy (moderate-severe illness)
Shake suspension well; confirm pediatric weight-based dose
Review concurrent QT-prolonging drugs before starting
moa: Macrolide that binds the 50S bacterial ribosomal subunit, inhibiting protein synthesis; bacteriostatic against susceptible organisms.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to azithromycin, erythromycin, any macrolide or ketolide
History of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction with prior azithromycin use
relative: Known QT prolongation or history of torsades de pointes

preg: No drug-associated risk identified in literature/postmarketing data; no malformations in animal studies.
lact: Present in human milk; non-serious infant reactions reported — use with caution.
renal: No adjustment in mild-moderate impairment; use caution in severe impairment (GFR <10 mL/min, ~35% AUC rise).
hepatic: Pharmacokinetics not established in hepatic impairment; contraindicated after prior cholestatic injury.

major: QT-prolonging drugs / antiarrhythmics — additive QT prolongation, torsades risk
Warfarin/oral anticoagulants — may potentiate effect; monitor prothrombin time
moderate: Nelfinavir — raises azithromycin levels; monitor for liver enzyme and hearing effects
Digoxin, colchicine, phenytoin — caution by macrolide class effect
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food (food raises Cmax but not overall exposure).

monitoring: ECG/QT in patients with cardiac risk or on QT-prolonging drugs
Liver function and signs of hepatitis
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed and finish the full course
Report rash, swelling, or trouble breathing immediately
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or severe abdominal pain
Report watery or bloody diarrhea, even weeks after stopping
Tell your doctor about heart-rhythm problems or other medicines
pearls: Very long ~68 h terminal half-life enables short 3-5 day courses
Single 1 g dose treats non-gonococcal urethritis/cervicitis and chancroid
Should not be used in pneumonia patients too ill for oral therapy
Carries QT-prolongation and torsades warning — caution with at-risk patients
IHPS reported in neonates treated up to 42 days of life
missed: Take as soon as remembered; skip if near next dose. Do not double.
overdose: Symptoms similar to normal doses (nausea, diarrhea, vomiting). Supportive and symptomatic care.
refs: U.S. FDA label via openFDA / DailyMed
